events.text: The ferryman who has taken your silver for nine years will not look at you this spring. The inn at Plum Ford has no rooms, and you can see the empty rooms from the road. It is only small things. A dog you know barks at you. Nobody has said a word, and that is the part you keep turning over.

choices.text: Ask the ferryman who told him not to look at you

ok.log: It takes a whole river and most of your dried persimmons. Somebody paid him, he says at last. Somebody paid everyone. He does not know the name, but he knows the silver was new.

fail.log: He looks at the water all the way over, and takes your fare without touching your hand.

choices.text: Let it go: it is a bad spring

effects.log: You let it go. It is a bad spring. It is followed by a bad summer.

events.text: Your favourite teahouse has started to serve you very good tea. The owner stands and watches you drink the first mouthful, and goes away. On the third visit you realise she is frightened. Someone has been in here, and asked her how often you come, and which seat. She does not know you have noticed. There is a new scratch on the underside of your table.

choices.text: Run a thumb along the scratch, and read it

ok.log: Whoever marked it used a court clerk's knife, and has done this before. It means there is a list somewhere, with your table on it. You pay, and leave a good tip, and start looking.

fail.log: It is just a scratch, you decide. You move to the seat by the window, and the tea stays very good.

choices.text: Change teahouses

effects.log: You change teahouses. In a month the new one has started serving very good tea.

events.text: Three letters you sent this year have arrived opened and closed again, by someone with a much better hand with wax than you have. An old friend mentions something you only ever told one other person. A beggar outside your gate this winter has very clean feet. None of it would stand up in front of anyone. You have not lived this long by waiting for things to stand up.

choices.text: Have the beggar followed

ok.log: You follow them yourself, over the roofs, as far as a house with very good locks. You do not go in. You know now that it is a house, and that it has been paid for.

fail.log: The beggar goes round one corner and is not there. Whoever taught that had taught it to many.

choices.text: Give the beggar a coin, and say nothing

effects.log: You give a coin. The beggar thanks you very politely, in the accent of a good school.

events.text: At a gathering this autumn, you come into a room and the talk does not stop. It goes on, smoothly, about the harvest. You have been in enough rooms to know how much work it takes for a whole table to go on talking about the harvest. {npc} looks up, and is the first to wish you good evening. {He} is very warm. {He} has never once been warm before.

choices.text: Sit down and talk about the harvest

ok.log: You talk harvest for an hour, and you watch who looks at who. By the end of it you could draw that table on a napkin, and you do, once you are home.

fail.log: You talk harvest for an hour, and you learn a great deal about the harvest.

choices.text: Leave early

effects.log: You leave early. Behind you, the talk gets easier. You can hear that from the stairs.

events.text: Someone has had a very accurate portrait made of you. You find this out because an old artist you once helped turns up at your door in tears, to tell you he did it, and that he was paid in advance, and that it took him a month, and that the buyer asked him to get the left shoulder right, the one you favour. He won't say who. He has a family.

choices.text: Thank him, and ask nothing more

effects.log: You give him tea and send him home. It is a useful thing to know, that someone has been studying your left shoulder. You begin to favour the other one.

choices.text: Press him for the name

effects.log: He weeps some more, and he tells you nothing, because he knows nothing. It is not a good evening for either of you.

events.text: A cousin of a friend, whom you barely know, stops you in the market and says that you should not take the mountain road this year. That is all. She has gone red to the ears. When you ask who told her so, she says that nobody did, and that she does not know what you are talking about, and that she has to go and see about some fish.

choices.text: Take the river road instead, and start asking why

effects.log: The river road is longer. Halfway along it you meet a charcoal burner who has seen a great many strangers on the mountain lately, all waiting for someone.

choices.text: Take the mountain road, as you always do

effects.log: Nothing happens on the mountain road, though you are watched the whole way. Somebody has learned that you do not take advice.

events.text: The report from the network is in your hand before breakfast. There is something the handler has underlined twice: silver moving in one direction, through four hands, for six years; and people who hate one another meeting at the same temple. {npc} is one name on it. There are others. The handler wants you to know this is not gossip. It has an order of business.

choices.text: Have them dig until you have every name

effects.log: You give the order. It will cost you some good people before it is done. The next report comes with no underlining, and it does not need any.

choices.text: Let it sit, and watch for a while

effects.log: You put it in the fire and you go to breakfast. You know something they do not know you know, and that is worth a little while.

events.text: One of the network's runners has died in a ditch outside Kaifeng with a page in her boot. They bring you the page. It is a seating plan, for a dinner of people who would not normally be seen together. {npc} is at the head of it. At the foot of it, in a careful hand, is a date, and your name, and the word "after."

choices.text: Find out what comes after

effects.log: You put more people on it. You also start paying the runner's mother, under some other name. You will want her to know, one day, what it bought.

choices.text: Burn the plan, and move your people

effects.log: You move everyone you can, overnight. Nobody at that dinner will know who you moved, or why. It does not tell you any more, but it costs them something.

events.text: Your rivals in the trade of secrets have sold you something, for a very fair price, with an air of doing you a favour. There is an alliance. It has been running for years. They think you ought to know, because it would be a great pity if your side lost you before they had finished beating you themselves. {npc} is mentioned on the second page.

choices.text: Pay, and read the rest

effects.log: You pay. It is worth every copper. It is a strange thing to be grateful to them, and you will get over it.

choices.text: Read the second page, and hand it back

effects.log: You read it twice and return it, with thanks. They laugh. It is as much as you were going to get for nothing, and you have a good memory.

events.text: {npc} has come a long way and will not come inside. It is someone you have known a long time, and they stand in the rain at the gate, and say it fast: there are people meeting about you. {He} has been asked, too. {He} was asked very nicely, and was told that everyone would be going along with it, and {he} should think of {his} family. {He} has thought about it, and here {he} is.

choices.text: Bring {him} in out of the rain

effects.log: {He} tells you what {he} knows, over something hot. It is not much, but there are names in it. It costs {him} a good deal more than it costs you.

mem.note: stood in the rain to warn me, and I had nothing to gain

choices.text: Thank {him}, and send {him} home by the back way

effects.log: {He} goes. You have someone left, it seems. That is worth knowing too, and so is the fact that they went to {him}.

events.text: It is {npc}, and it is late, and it is a very odd time for {him} to be bringing back the book {he} borrowed nine years ago. There is a note in the book. {He} does not mention it. {He} talks about the weather, and looks at the walls of your room, and {he} asks after your health in a way {he} never has before. Then {he} goes. You read the note.

choices.text: Read it, and burn it

effects.log: It says who has been to see {him}, and when, in that very small handwriting of {his}. You burn it. You will not ever be able to thank {him} for this.

choices.text: Leave it in the book, and send the book back

effects.log: You send it back with a note of your own: one word. {He} will know what it means. You are both safer if nobody else does.

events.text: You find {npc} on your roof, drunk and in tears, which you have never seen before and did not expect. {He} has been told something about you, and has been told how well things are going to go for {him} when it is over. {He} wants to know if it is true that you once did what they say you did. {He} wants you to tell {him} that you did not.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth

effects.log: You tell {him}, sitting on the tiles. It is not all good. {He} sobers up as you talk, and by morning {he} has told you all of it, every name that {he} heard.

choices.text: Get {him} down off the roof, and ask nothing

effects.log: You get {him} down and to bed. In the morning {he} is gone, with a nod. Somebody out there has lost a friend tonight, and it was not you.

events.text: You have it all at last, spread out on one table. It is an alliance, and there are more of them than you thought: {hnt_names}. {npc} is the one who planned it. {hnt_origin} You have been the only thing they have talked about for years. All you need now is to decide what to do about it, and you have one advantage: they think you do not know.

choices.text: Go to {npc} first, before they can move

effects.log: You put down the papers and you pick up your sword. Some things do not need a meeting.

choices.text: Send {npc} a price

effects.log: You name a figure. Everyone has one, and you have always found the people who say they do not are the most expensive.

choices.text: Let them spring it, and be ready

effects.log: You send word, the careful kind, of where you will be next year. They will be so pleased.

choices.text: Sit on it, and watch them

effects.log: You put it all away. You are going to enjoy the next few dinners, in your way.

events.text: The last piece is a stable boy who saw who came to the temple at Longmen, and it turns out there is no last piece: there is a whole picture, and you have been looking at it for years. {hnt_names}. You know some of those people. You have eaten with some of them. {hnt_origin} {npc} sits at the middle of it, and has been writing to you at New Year.

choices.text: Answer the New Year letter in person

effects.log: You will deliver this one yourself.

choices.text: Send a very generous New Year gift

effects.log: It is the most expensive gift you have ever sent. You enclose a list of what you know, in case that helps with the thank-you note.

choices.text: Accept the next invitation they send

effects.log: There is one coming. There would have to be. You write back that you would be delighted.

choices.text: Go on writing at New Year

effects.log: You write back the same as always, in the same hand. You are becoming quite good at it.

events.text: It is an ordinary evening when it all comes together, over bad soup, in a room with a single lamp. Each of those people had a reason. You can see every one. {hnt_names}. {hnt_origin} It is almost a relief, like finding out what the pain in your side has been called all this time. {npc} has been very patient, and very clever. You find you respect it. You will still have to do something.

choices.text: Finish the soup, and go and see {npc}

effects.log: You finish the soup. It would be a shame to waste it, and {npc} is not going anywhere.

choices.text: Find out what {npc} really wants

effects.log: Nobody plans for this long for nothing. You have the figure drawn up by morning.

choices.text: Walk straight into the trap

effects.log: It is a good trap. It would be a shame to waste that as well.

choices.text: Do nothing for now

effects.log: You blow out the lamp. They do not know that you know. You have not had an advantage this good in years.

events.text: Someone has bought you a gift of a list. It is delivered by the youngest person on it, who cannot look at you, and who has plainly stopped being able to sleep. {hnt_names}. {hnt_origin} {npc} is the one who keeps it all going, the youngster says, and {he} never raises {his} voice. Then the youngster runs. You have the whole thing in your hand now, and it only weighs what a sheet of paper weighs.

choices.text: Pay {npc} a visit

effects.log: You do not hurry. You have waited this long without knowing it, and now you are the one with time.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a way out, at a price

effects.log: You send the offer through someone that {npc} trusts. That person will be surprised to find out who they really work for.

choices.text: Let the trap close on you

effects.log: You make sure that they can find you. It is a lot harder to be careless on purpose than you would think.

choices.text: Let the youngster run, and wait

effects.log: You let them run. Whoever else is losing sleep will come to you, in time.

events.text: The story has reached the far provinces before you heard it: that you did not win your great victory. That your opponent was poisoned. There are details. It is very good work, and {npc} has been heard to defend you against it, loudly, at great length, in front of as many people as possible, in a way that makes it sound much worse.

choices.text: Find the first teller of it

ok.log: It takes a season, and it leads you from a storyteller to a printer to a steward in {npc}'s pay. You leave the storyteller a better story to tell.

fail.log: Each teller had it from another. It is a lovely piece of work. There is no first teller to be found.

choices.text: Answer it with a public duel

effects.log: You fight in the open, with anyone who wants to try. Nobody can say that was poison, and they say other things instead.

choices.text: Say nothing

effects.log: You say nothing. A great many people take that to mean what you would expect.

events.text: A ballad has started going around about someone very like you, who sold out a friend for a manual. It has a good tune. Children are singing it. {npc} has paid for it to be sung in nine cities, and you have heard it twice already this week. The second time was in your own kitchen, where the cook stopped very suddenly when you came in.

choices.text: Learn it, and sing it at the next banquet

effects.log: You have a terrible voice. The whole hall freezes through the second verse, then someone starts laughing, and it never sounds quite the same after that.

choices.text: Find out who has been paying the singers

ok.log: A singer who owes you a kindness tells you, over a bowl of noodles, whose steward it is. You leave her enough to learn a different song.

fail.log: The singers close up when you come near. You hear it again on your way out, sung a little louder.

choices.text: Let them sing

effects.log: They sing. It is very catchy. Twenty years from now, you will still hear it in places.

events.text: A respected old monk has said, in public, with sorrow, that he fears for your soul. He does not say why, and he does not have to. {npc} has been sending him rice for years. People now lower their voices when you come by, and they look at you with something like pity. It is much harder to hit pity than it is to hit anger.

choices.text: Go and sit with the monk, and ask what he fears

ok.log: He is honest and he has been lied to. You sit with him for three days. He does not take it back in public, but he stops saying it, and he tells you who brought the rice.

fail.log: He looks at you with such sorrow that you find you have nothing to say. People see you leaving, and that gets told too.

choices.text: Build the monk a new roof, and say nothing

effects.log: It costs you, and it is a good roof. It would be very hard to go on fearing for the soul of the person who paid for it.

choices.text: Let the old fool talk

effects.log: You say that, and someone hears you say that.

events.text: A false you has been going around. Your height, your walk, your scar, and a very good copy of your sword. In the last year, you have robbed a temple and insulted a governor and failed to pay at nine inns, and {npc} has very kindly offered to help you make it right, in front of all the people you have wronged. Someone has clearly studied you.

choices.text: Hunt down the false you

ok.log: You corner a tired actor in a barn, with very good shoulders. He is relieved. He has a contract, in writing, and he is happy to show you who signed it.

fail.log: You are a day behind them for a whole winter, paying for things you did not do.

choices.text: Pay at all nine inns, and let it be known

effects.log: It costs you, and now everyone knows the real one pays. It does not stop the false one, but it makes them less fun.

choices.text: Laugh it off

effects.log: You laugh it off, and that is also what a person who did it would do.

events.text: The magistrate of Luoyang has a sworn statement, three witnesses and a bloodstained token with your mark on it, all concerning a merchant you never met. Constables stand at your door looking as if they would much rather be elsewhere. {npc} has already called on the magistrate, to say what a shock it all is.

choices.text: Pick the case apart in open court

ok.log: The token is two years newer than the date on the statement, and you make the court look at it for a long time. The witnesses have stopped remembering things. You also get a name.

fail.log: It is a very well built case. You come out with a fine, a long record and your name on the board outside.

choices.text: Go with them quietly, and answer it from a cell

effects.log: You go in on your own feet, and you stay in, whatever you could do to that door. It is two hard years, but every witness has to come and look you in the eye, and the case falls apart. Nobody can say you ran.

choices.text: Pay what the magistrate wants

effects.log: It goes away, and now there is a magistrate who has been paid by you, and {npc} knows how much.

choices.text: Leave town, and let them say what they want

effects.log: You leave town. They say what they want. It stays on the board outside the yamen for ten years.

events.text: A shipment of something very illegal has been found in a warehouse rented in your name, in your handwriting. The landlord swears to your face. Hours before, someone tipped off the salt inspectors, and {npc} is one of those who has come along to see, looking very grave, with a good view of the door.

choices.text: Find whoever rented it, with your own hands

ok.log: You go through the docks one door at a time, and you bring the real renter to the inspectors by the collar. They are astonished, and {npc} is especially astonished.

fail.log: The docks have closed their mouths. The inspectors write it all down, and heat follows you for years.

choices.text: Let the inspectors search everything you own

effects.log: They find nothing, which takes them two years and makes you look clean. It also lets them read everything you own.

choices.text: Walk away from it

effects.log: You walk away. They are very happy to have the warehouse, and your handwriting.

events.text: A young woman has come forward at the Governor's gate to say that you killed her father eleven years ago. She is sincere. Somebody has spent years making sure of it. She has a letter, in what she believes is your hand, and {npc} has taken her in, and has paid for her lawyer, and stands beside her at the gate looking stricken.

choices.text: Speak to her, alone

ok.log: It takes you a long time, and she does not stop hating you. But she shows you the letter, and she has a good eye: she notices the year on the paper for herself. She goes home a lot quieter than she came.

fail.log: She spits at your feet, and everybody sees it. There is nothing you can say to her that sounds like anything other than what it sounds like.

choices.text: Answer it at the Governor's court, from the cells if need be

effects.log: You go in and you stay in, though no cell in that city could hold you if you meant it. It takes two years to prove what she was told is a lie. You do not ask her to forgive you. She visits once, near the end.

choices.text: Have nothing to do with it

effects.log: You have nothing to do with it. She tells it in every town from there to the sea.

events.text: A body was found at your door this morning. It is a clerk of the salt office, and you have never seen them before, and they have your seal in their sleeve. The neighbours heard you arguing last night, all of them, in the same words. {npc} was first on the scene, with a physician, and with the constables close behind.

choices.text: Help the constables, and look at the body yourself

effects.log: Dead for three days, you point out, and moved in a cart. The physician agrees, unhappily. It does not clear you, but it is told in the right ears.

choices.text: Get to the neighbours before anyone else does

ok.log: It turns out that all of them were paid by the same man, in the same copper. One of them still has the string. It was tied by someone who works for {npc}.

fail.log: They stick to it. You have now also been seen leaning on witnesses.

choices.text: Bury the clerk yourself, and say nothing

effects.log: You pay for a decent burial for someone who deserved one, and let people say what they will. They do.

events.text: There is a warrant out in three counties for a crime with a very long name, in connection with some old debts of yours. All of it is true on paper. You signed each page for reasons that made sense at the time. {npc} has spent six years buying up every one of those pages, and has now handed them all in at once.

choices.text: Pay them all, at once, in front of the yamen

effects.log: You have it carted in. It takes most of a day to count, and the whole town comes to watch. {npc} sends a note of congratulation.

choices.text: Read every page, and find the mistake

ok.log: Page forty is dated on a holiday. It is not much, but it brings the whole stack down, and it tells you who was buying.

fail.log: There is no mistake. They paid good people to make sure of that.

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: You go on as usual. The warrant goes on too, a little ahead of you in every town.

events.text: A sealed box, a dead courier, and in the box the plans of a city gate with your notes in the margin: treason, by the look of it. The commandant of the garrison has taken it to the Censorate. {npc} has come by to tell you in person. {He} has always been so sure that you would never do such a thing, {he} says, and {he} is telling everyone so.

choices.text: Go to the Censorate before they send for you

ok.log: You walk in with your hands open, and sit down, and ask to see the notes. The handwriting is excellent. It is also someone else's, and you know whose school taught it.

fail.log: You walk in with your hands open, and you are treated very well, and nothing you say is written down.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let it blow over

effects.log: It does not blow over. It goes into a drawer, with your name on it. It will come back out when somebody needs it.

events.text: Forty censors have knelt outside the palace gate since dawn, in the snow, with a memorial charging you with nine crimes against heaven. Most of them believe it. Their old teacher has been receiving very handsome letters from {npc}. It is a great deal easier to arrest a rebel than a kneeling man in the snow, and everybody on that side of the wall has worked that out.

choices.text: Have braziers and hot soup brought out to them

effects.log: You send it all, with your own compliments. It is the only answer they cannot put in the next memorial. Half of them drink it, and the other half never forgive them.

choices.text: Read all nine charges aloud, and answer each one

ok.log: You do it in the open, on the steps, in the cold. By the sixth, some of them are not sure. By the ninth, one has asked who wrote this for them.

fail.log: You read them aloud. They are very well written. Your voice carries all of them across the whole city.

choices.text: Have them removed

effects.log: They are removed, carefully, and it is written down by the ones who were not. That is what they came for.

events.text: An eclipse is coming, and the Astronomer Royal has been found to have read in it the misrule of the throne. He has never before been so sure of anything. He has also been dining with {npc}. The city has begun to store water, and the ministers look at you, and then at the sky, and then they look at each other.

choices.text: Hold the rites yourself, and take the blame on yourself

effects.log: You fast three days, you kneel in the open and you ask heaven's pardon, in simple words. The sun comes back. People who were there say that they saw it listen.

choices.text: Have his sums checked by someone else

ok.log: A young clerk in the bureau finds it in an hour, and shakes while she shows you. It has been written in after, in someone else's hand. You ask her to take a look at his dinner guests.

fail.log: His sums are good. It really is an eclipse. There is nothing else to find.

choices.text: Dismiss him

effects.log: You dismiss him, and the eclipse comes anyway, just as he said it would.

events.text: Grain riots in the south, and then, within a week, in the west, the same words on the same banners. It is cleverly done, says {npc}, in council, with tears in {his} eyes. If only the granaries had been opened sooner. Everyone at the table knows who kept them shut. They were shut on the advice of someone at this table.

choices.text: Open the granaries, whatever it costs

effects.log: You open them, all of them. It costs what it costs. The riots stop in the south, and in the west they have some trouble explaining what the banners are for now.

choices.text: Send the army

effects.log: The army goes. It does what armies do. It is a very quiet province after that, and you do not get to go there any more.

events.text: {npc} has been coming back late. {He} has new boots, very good ones, and {he} has begun to ask you questions that a student does not usually ask: which road you plan to take; whether the old wound still hurts in the cold. {He} does it badly. You taught {him} everything {he} knows, and you did not teach {him} that.

choices.text: Ask {him}, straight out, who bought the boots

ok.log: There is a long silence, and then {he} kneels down and tells you. They came to {him} a year ago. {He} has told them nothing that was true. {He} has been so frightened. You help {him} up.

fail.log: {He} looks you in the eye and says an uncle gave them to {him}. {He} has learned that part, at least. You go on teaching {him}.

choices.text: Say nothing, and trust {him}

effects.log: You say nothing. You have always told them that a master who cannot trust is only a person with a stick. You will find out.

choices.text: Send {him} away

effects.log: You send {him} away that night, with a purse. {He} weeps and swears {he} did nothing. You will never know, and you will always think about it.

events.text: Someone has been telling {npc} what you really said about {him}, to the elders, years ago. Some of it is even true. You watch {him} go quiet through the winter, and {he} is very correct with you, and {he} no longer laughs at the things that {he} used to. Someone has taken a great deal of trouble over this. It is very hard to fight something you actually said.

choices.text: Tell {him} exactly what you said, and why

effects.log: You sit {him} down and go through it, every word. It is the worst evening you have spent in years. {He} does not forgive you. But {he} stays, and {he} tells you who has been talking to {him}.

choices.text: Give {him} room, and leave it alone

effects.log: You give {him} room. It is a very respectful kind of silence. You will find out, later, what it was full of.

events.text: A scroll has gone from your room, and {npc} was the only one who knew where you kept it. {He} brings you your tea as usual. {His} hands are quite steady. It may have been someone else. There are a dozen other ways it could have happened, and you can list them, and you do, and you drink your tea.

choices.text: Set a test: tell {him} alone something false

ok.log: What you told {him} never turns up anywhere. The scroll was taken by someone else, in the end. You are very ashamed of yourself, and {he} never needs to know.

fail.log: What you told {him} turns up in a month, in the wrong mouth. {He} still brings your tea. {His} hands are very steady.

choices.text: Let it go: you trained those hands

effects.log: You let it go. You trained those hands. You will find out what you trained them for.

events.text: They have offered {npc} a sect of {his} own, when it is all over. {He} comes and tells you so, at once, with the letter in {his} hand, and {he} is white in the face. It is what {he} has always wanted, and you both know it. And now that {he} has told you, {he} has to go back and tell them something. {He} asks what {he} should do.

choices.text: Have {him} go on meeting them, for you

effects.log: It is a terrible thing to ask, and you ask it. {He} goes. Every month {he} tells you what they said, and {he} gets a little older every time.

mem.note: asked me to go back among them, and I went

choices.text: Tell {him} to decide for {him}self

effects.log: You tell {him} that it is {his} life, and you mean it. {He} looks at you for a while, and goes. You do not know which way.

events.text: {npc}, who is the best you ever taught, has been heard to say that a teacher who stays at the top for this long is standing on someone. It is a thing that a clever person says at that age, and you may have said it yourself. But it has been repeated with care in the right rooms, and now the younger ones have started to look at {him} instead of you when you speak.

choices.text: Spar with {him}, in front of all of them, and lose if you must

ok.log: You give {him} the bout of {his} life, and you give {him} the credit too. By the end {he} is laughing, the way {he} used to. There is no more talk about standing on anyone.

fail.log: {He} is better than you thought, and {he} has been getting advice. You hold your own, barely. The younger ones saw everything.

choices.text: Hear {him} out, in private

effects.log: {He} says it all to your face, and it is quite well argued. You thank {him}. It is hard to say which of you is more surprised.

events.text: Your best customer has stopped paying. So has your second best. The tea you shipped in spring arrived in the north with a fine grey mould that nobody has ever seen on tea, and the buyers have all been told about it by someone with a very sympathetic manner. {npc} has offered to take the whole business off your hands, at a price, as a friend.

choices.text: Go through the books, and the ships, yourself

ok.log: The mould was put on at the third warehouse, by a man who was paid in advance. You keep the customers, and you take his name to someone who can read it.

fail.log: You find the loss, and you never find where it went. It goes on being lost.

choices.text: Make the buyers whole, out of your own pocket

effects.log: It costs you, and every buyer in the north hears that you made it right before they asked. They keep ordering, out of plain surprise.

choices.text: Let it ride

effects.log: You let it ride. The season closes, and it is a much smaller business than it was.

events.text: A man with a pleasant face has been going around your people, one at a time. Your manager has had an offer. So have the carters. The offer is very good, and the only thing it asks is that they do slightly less, for a while. {npc} is said to be behind it. You notice all this when your ledgers begin to come in beautifully neat, and very late.

choices.text: Match the offer, for everyone, in public

effects.log: You stand on a crate, in the yard, and name the figure. They cheer, and it hurts. The man with the pleasant face moves on to some other town.

choices.text: Find out who they already took

ok.log: A carter tells you, over a cup, because you once paid for his mother's physician. You know now who to watch, and who hired them.

fail.log: Everyone is very loyal, and very neat. The business comes in a little lighter each quarter.

choices.text: Trust your people

effects.log: You trust your people. Most of them deserve it. The rest have new boots.

events.text: Your whole trade goes through one bridge, and it has been condemned by the county as unsafe. There is nothing wrong with that bridge. The engineer who signed the paper has just bought a house. The next bridge is forty miles on, and it belongs to a friend of {npc}, who would be very glad to quote you a price.

choices.text: Walk across it in front of the whole county, with a loaded cart

ok.log: You do it twice, the second time with the county magistrate on top of the cart, looking ill. The paper is withdrawn.

fail.log: The cart gets halfway, and a wheel has been loosened. The whole county sees it go over. It is exactly what they said would happen.

choices.text: Pay the forty miles, and keep going

effects.log: You pay. Your costs go up, and theirs go down, and you have not stopped.

choices.text: Let the trade stop for a season

effects.log: It stops for a season, and so do your customers, some of them for good.

events.text: A very large order has come in, and it is the sort of order that makes your whole year. You have borrowed to fill it. Now it has been cancelled, with regrets, by a buyer who turns out to have been dead for six years, and all your loans have been called in together, by a bank in which {npc} has lately taken an interest. It took someone a very long time to build this.

choices.text: Sell what you must, and pay it all

effects.log: You sell off the good warehouse at a bad price. You are smaller, you are clean, and you owe nobody. It is possible they did not expect that.

choices.text: Go and see the bank in person

ok.log: You sit down across from the manager and you read aloud, slowly, the name of the dead buyer. He goes very pale. He extends the loan, and asks you not to say where you heard it.

fail.log: He is very polite. He has been told that you would come, and what you would say.

events.text: Six people with good shoes come for you on the road below Mount Song, and they do not say anything at all. Professionals. Somebody paid for them in advance and told them exactly what you can do. You recognise one of the forms they use, from an old fight, in which {npc} stood on your left and watched very closely.

choices.text: Fight them

ok.log: It is ugly and it is short. You keep one breathing long enough to go through the purse, and it holds a coin from the mint that {npc} has been buying from.

fail.log: They knew about the shoulder. You get away by jumping off something, and you are a long time mending.

choices.text: Get out of there

effects.log: You go over the cliff and through the river. You lose a good coat, and they have learned how you run.

events.text: Your cook has been replaced with someone who has a very good knife hand. You notice this during the soup. Your new cook notices you noticing. It is a small kitchen. Somebody has told them you never eat anything before you have looked at it, and so {npc} must have had dinner with you, at some point, and been watching.

choices.text: Settle it, here in the kitchen

ok.log: It takes a while to clean up. You have a fairly good idea now of who has been to dinner, and you have made soup for yourself, which is terrible.

fail.log: They go out through the window with your good knife, and leave a long cut behind on your forearm.

choices.text: Compliment the soup, and leave by the back

effects.log: You compliment the soup. You leave by the back. You will need a new cook, and a new kitchen, and you will not be sleeping here again.

events.text: Somebody has sent a very famous killer to you, with an appointment. Word comes first, and the date, because that one has a reputation for manners. Half the province has started to lay out silver on how it goes, and {npc} has made sure you heard that {he} is thinking of you at this difficult time.

choices.text: Keep the appointment

ok.log: They bow at the end of it, from the ground. They tell you who hired them, because they were not told to keep it quiet, and because they have manners.

fail.log: They stop one move short, and bow, and let you up. "Paid to frighten," they say. "It is a very strange contract. I would look to your friends."

choices.text: Be somewhere else that day

effects.log: You are somewhere else. It costs you nothing but the whole province's opinion.

events.text: Somebody has been in the ear of the house you sit in. {npc} has been dining with the upper table, and now the elders of the blood look at you, then at each other, as they did when you first came. A list of what you have asked for, these last few years, has been going around. It has been very nicely copied out.

choices.text: Go before them, and read the list aloud yourself

effects.log: You read it, every favour, with the date. It is hard to whisper about something after it has been read aloud at dinner. They count you all the same.

choices.text: Say nothing, and keep your head down

effects.log: You keep your head down. It does not look as modest from above as it feels from inside.

events.text: A letter has reached the head of the house you sit in, unsigned, setting out what you are really after. Most of it is wrong. A few lines are not. You know this, because the steward has stopped looking you in the eye, and because you know now that someone like {npc} has been going through your laundry for a good few years.

choices.text: Find the steward's price

ok.log: It is only his son's debts. You pay them. He tells you who brought the letter, and how it was folded.

fail.log: He does not have a price, or else he has a better one. He looks at you very sadly.

choices.text: Let the letter do what it does

effects.log: You let it. They read it. They start to count, and the count goes up.

events.text: {npc} has made a friend of the most stupid of the young of the house, and has taught {him}self a few of their jokes. Now that young idiot has challenged you, in the yard, in front of everyone, on a point of honour that somebody had to write out for {him}. If you lose, you look weak. If you win, you have hurt the family. Someone has thought about this.

choices.text: Win so kindly that it looks like a lesson

ok.log: You let the youngster look good for nine moves and then you sit them down, gently, in a puddle. Even the aunts laugh. You go up in their eyes, and it was a close thing.

fail.log: You win. Nobody laughs. You have hurt a child of the name, in public, and it is written down.

choices.text: Decline, and take the talk that follows

effects.log: You bow, and decline. They call you afraid, and it costs you, and nobody of the blood has been hurt.

events.text: Doors you used to walk through have started being shut. Not slammed. The Alliance has no record of your invitation. The Beggars have nothing to report. {npc} has had a quiet word in a lot of places, to the effect that it would be better for everyone if you were left alone, and everyone has understood that to mean exactly what it means.

choices.text: Go to each door anyway, and knock

effects.log: You go to each one, in person, in daylight. They do not open, but everybody sees who is standing outside, and some of them are ashamed.

choices.text: Find one door that will still open

ok.log: An old woman who sells noodles to the whole jianghu has never cared what anyone says. She tells you who has been round, and she charges you for the noodles.

fail.log: They are all very sorry. Even the noodle seller looks at her hands.

choices.text: Go where there are no doors

effects.log: You go off to the far hills for a while. It is a kind of answer. Nobody down there has to hear it.

events.text: You are not anyone's to expel, so they have found another way: every sect in the region has been asked to swear they will give you no shelter, by {npc}, on behalf of some very respectable elders. It sounds like a formality. You find out that it is not when you come down off the mountain in a blizzard, and a gate that you once saved stays shut.

choices.text: Spend the night in the blizzard, under their wall

effects.log: You sit under their wall all night. In the morning, a young disciple comes out with hot congee and is punished for it. You will remember that young person's name.

choices.text: Get over the wall, and take it up with their elders

ok.log: You appear at breakfast, with snow on you, and take a seat. The elders explain, in some detail, who asked them. You thank them for the rice.

fail.log: You appear at breakfast, with snow on you. They all look at you. Nobody tells you anything at all.

events.text: There is a story in the jianghu that you are finished. That your old wounds have got you. That you are hiding out. The young have started coming to test you, one every few months, each with a letter of introduction from someone respectable. {npc} wrote most of those letters. {He} is very free with them. {He} knows that you do not like to hurt children.

choices.text: Send each of them home with a lesson

effects.log: They go home thoughtful, with all their fingers, and some of them come back later to thank you. It does nothing to the story, but it does a lot for the young.

choices.text: Stop answering the door

effects.log: You stop answering. The story has a new chapter by the end of the month.

events.text: The council you answer to has been asked to review your record. It is purely routine. {npc} has been very good to several of the people who will read it. Your merit has been found to be slightly miscounted. Your last promotion may have been a clerical error. Your rivals have begun to bow to you much more deeply than they did.

choices.text: Go before the council, and answer it

ok.log: You bring your own count, with witnesses. It takes three days, and they apologise, in writing. On the third day an old elder takes you aside to tell you who asked.

fail.log: They hear you out very courteously. The review finds what it was set up to find.

choices.text: Accept the review

effects.log: You accept it, with a bow. It costs you a lot of what you earned, and it looks very humble from a distance.

events.text: You have been given a great honour: the post at the northern pass, in command of everything. It is a long way off. It is a very cold place, the supply road washes out each spring, and the last three people who held it did not come back. {npc} made the speech proposing you, and it was a very good speech. Everyone stood up.

choices.text: Find a reason, in the rules, that you cannot go

ok.log: Regulation nine. Nobody has read it in sixty years. An old clerk finds it for you, and tells you, while he is at it, who paid for the speech.

fail.log: Regulation nine was amended last spring. You go north for two winters, and come back with fewer toes than you had, and far less merit.

choices.text: Go, and do it well

effects.log: You go and hold the pass, and the supply road, and it is hard, and you bring everyone back. That was not in the plan. Nobody thanks you for it, and many people notice.

events.text: A junior of yours has been promoted over you. You taught them to tie their belt. It has been done very correctly, on the advice of the outer elders, and {npc} has sent you a very warm note about it. Now you must bow to them in the yard each morning, and you can feel everyone watching, to see how long you will stand it.

choices.text: Bow each morning, properly, and help them

effects.log: You bow. You help. Some mornings it is the hardest thing you do. In a year that junior is coming to you at night for advice, and in two years they are telling you what they hear.

choices.text: Bow, and say nothing, and wait

effects.log: You bow and you say nothing. It eats up a lot of what you used to have, and it does not get easier.

events.text: You are accused, in full council, of plotting against the head of your house, which is a thing that a lot of people have been told you must be doing. {npc} is very sorry to be bringing it up. There are letters. You did not write them, but somebody has written a good many and has clearly enjoyed it.

choices.text: Ask to have them read out in full

ok.log: They are very long, and on the fourth page they use a word you never use, and on the sixth they call someone by a name that was only given to them last year. The room begins to shift.

fail.log: They are read out in full. It takes the whole of the afternoon, and every word is about you.

choices.text: Throw yourself on the head's mercy

effects.log: You kneel, and it is noted. You are forgiven, and the forgiving costs you everything you have earned here for years.

events.text: A delegation has come to see you, from among your own. They would like you to know how grateful they are. They are worried about your health. They think you have been carrying too much for too long, and {npc}, who has been so kind to all of them lately, agrees. There is a very nice mountain they have found for you to retire to.

choices.text: Thank them, and ask to see the mountain

effects.log: You go and look at it with them, and walk them around it for three days. By the end they have begun to feel foolish, and two of them tell you who suggested it.

choices.text: Send them away

effects.log: You send them away, a little sharply. They go home and tell everyone exactly how you took it.

events.text: There is a second teacher in your house now. Nobody appointed them. They give very good advice and they make no claim to anything, and {npc} speaks highly of them, and half of those you lead have started to take their troubles to that room rather than yours. You have heard that it is a very pleasant room. They always have time.

choices.text: Go and sit in that room yourself

ok.log: You sit there one whole afternoon, as a student. They are honest, as it turns out, and they had no idea who was paying their rent. They are appalled. Now they work for you.

fail.log: They are charming to you, and you come out having said more than you meant to.

choices.text: Ignore it: they will come back

effects.log: Some of them do. It takes a very long time, and the ones who do not come back all know each other.

events.text: Your house has an old law about who can hold the seal, and nobody has read it since the day you wrote it. Somebody has read it now. It seems that you broke it, slightly, nine years ago, over a boundary. {npc} has very gently brought it to the notice of the elders. They would hate to make anything of it. You wrote that law yourself, in a hurry, and you can see the mistake from here.

choices.text: Stand up, and pay the penalty you wrote

effects.log: You read your own law aloud, and you pay your own fine, in front of them all, and you add a line to it. Nobody will ever bring it up again, and everyone there has seen you do it.

choices.text: Change the law

effects.log: You have the power to change it, and you do. It is the end of the matter, and the beginning of a rather different one.

events.text: A branch of your people has gone quiet. Their letters are correct and they are late, and they have started using a new word for you that is one rung less than what they used before. {npc} has opened a very good market near them. The trouble is not that they have rebelled. The trouble is that nobody is able to say whether they have.

choices.text: Go there, unannounced

ok.log: You turn up for the evening meal. It is hard to be one rung less than someone who is passing you the pickles. By the third day you know everything, and who has been selling them salt.

fail.log: They are delighted to see you. Everything is in very good order. You leave with no idea what you have just seen.

choices.text: Leave them to it

effects.log: You leave them to it. They do not rebel. They just stop being there, by degrees.

events.text: Your chief minister has fallen ill, at a very useful moment, and his deputy turns out to be a person who was recommended by {npc}. In the first month he finds that some of the palace accounts do not add up. He comes to you with this, in private, deeply concerned. He has already told the Grand Secretary, who is also deeply concerned.

choices.text: Have the accounts brought, and read them in open court

ok.log: They do not add up, and you show the court why: it is his own copying. He has the grace to faint. There is a letter in his sleeve, and you find it most interesting.

fail.log: They do not add up. Nothing you can say in open court will make them add up. It is not a good day.

choices.text: Visit the sick minister

effects.log: You go in person, with soup. He is not as ill as all that. He cries, and then he tells you who told him to go to bed.

events.text: The generals are being invited to dinner. It is nothing, it is just that each of them, one at a time, has been dining with {npc}, who has been asking about their pensions and how they feel about the northern command. You know this because one of them came to tell you. You do not know how many have not.

choices.text: Double the pensions, and hold a review

effects.log: You ride down the whole line in full view, and each man gets his silver from your own hand. It is very expensive. They cheer, and you have no way of telling.

choices.text: Rotate the commands, at once

effects.log: It breaks up whatever it was, and everything else too. Nobody has any idea, now, who commands what, and that includes you.

events.text: A prince of an old line has been found. He is very young and very handsome, and he has a jade token and a good story, and he is living very quietly with {npc}. Nobody has said he has any claim. Nobody has to. The old families have started sending him gifts for the New Year. The children in the street have a new song.

choices.text: Invite him to court, with honour

ok.log: He comes, and you are kind. He is seventeen, and terrified, and he has no idea what he is for. He tells you everything in a week. You find him a nice post, far away.

fail.log: He comes, and he is magnificent, and the whole court falls in love. You have just shown him to everybody.

choices.text: Have the token examined, quietly

effects.log: It is genuine. Of course it is. It only took somebody thirty years to arrange.

events.text: You go to {npc} yourself, at the hour when the guards change, by the way nobody thinks of. {He} is sitting up, with a lamp and a pot of tea and two cups. {He} has always thought that you might come. "Well," {he} says. "Sit down, or get on with it. I find I do not much mind which."

choices.text: Get on with it, and leave nobody to talk

ok.log: It is very quiet when you leave. You wash the second cup, for no reason, and put it back. By morning they will all know that there is one less at the table.

fail.log: {He} has not been sitting up alone. You go out through the roof with more holes in your coat than you came in with, and now they know you know.

choices.text: Sit down, and take {him} out of it

ok.log: You drink the tea. You talk until dawn. {He} sends a letter at sunrise saying {he} has been unwell and will not be at the next meeting, or any other.

fail.log: {He} smiles and pours you more. You leave knowing a little less than you did. They know a little more.

events.text: You catch {npc} on the road, with six guards and a very good horse. They saw you first. The guards look at you, and at each other, and then at the money they are being paid. {npc} sits up straight in the saddle. It is an excellent piece of bearing, and you would have liked to know {him} better.

choices.text: Go through all of them

ok.log: The horse is the only one that does not run, and it stands over {him} until you take it by the bridle. You leave the road as you found it, and you send the horse home.

fail.log: They were paid better than you thought. You get clear, but {he} is laughing at you, and you can hear it for a good way.

choices.text: Have a word with the guards

ok.log: You name a figure, and you say it loud enough. In a little while {npc} is sitting on a very good horse, alone, on an empty road. You let {him} ride home. {He} is finished, and {he} knows it.

fail.log: They laugh. They have been told you would say that, and what you would offer.

events.text: It does not have to be a sword. You have spent a month on {npc}'s affairs. {He} owes too much to too many, and a very small push in three places would bring it all down around {him}, quite lawfully, by the end of the summer. You could also just go and see {him}. It is a fine evening and you know the road.

choices.text: Make the three small pushes

ok.log: It comes down like wet paper, all by itself, by harvest. {He} never finds out who did it, and {he} has better things to think about now than you.

fail.log: Two of the pushes work. The third was being watched. {He} loses a good deal, and {he} knows exactly who to thank.

choices.text: Go and see {him}

ok.log: You go and see {him}. It is a fine evening. Nobody else will be getting a letter from {him} after this.

fail.log: {He} has been expecting that, for some time. You come home on foot and on one good leg.

events.text: They meet at the temple on the last night of each month. You could be there first. {npc} comes early, alone, to check the doors, and {he} has checked the doors every month for years, because {he} is careful. You are on the roof beams when {he} comes in with {his} lantern. {He} does the doors, one at a time, and comes to stand directly beneath you.

choices.text: Drop

ok.log: Nobody finds out for a day. Then there is a very awkward meeting, with an empty place at the table and nobody willing to say what they think that means. You have been thinking about the look of that empty place for a long time.

fail.log: A beam creaks. {He} looks up. {He} does not shout. {He} just looks at you, and blows out the lantern, and in the dark you can hear {him} leaving.

choices.text: Let {him} go, and hear what they have to say

effects.log: You stay up there all night, with a stiff neck. You hear everything. They are very clever, and it is a long list, and you are going to enjoy being the one person who has read it.

events.text: The silver goes in a plain box, and you carry it yourself. {npc} opens it, and looks for a while, and shuts it again. "Do you know," {he} says, "I have been hoping for years that you would try this. It would have been a lot cheaper the first time." {He} does not touch it, and {he} does not push it back.

choices.text: Say that is all there is, and there is no second box

effects.log: {He} nods slowly. You leave the box with {him}. You will not know until it matters what you have bought.

choices.text: Say you know about the son, and leave it at that

effects.log: You say only that. {His} face does not change. {He} moves the box a little closer to {him}self. It is not a nice thing that you have done, and it may hold.

events.text: It is very simple in the end: a meeting in a boat, no witnesses, a very old debt of {npc}'s bought up and burned in front of {him}, and a good sum after that. {He} watches the paper burn all the way down. {He} has hated you for years, and {he} has come to think that this is a reason. {He} is finding out what the reason was worth.

choices.text: Tell {him} you know what it is worth to be hated, and row back

effects.log: You row back. {He} is sitting quite still. You think that one might hold.

choices.text: Have {him} sign something

effects.log: {He} signs. It would ruin {him} if you showed it. It would also make a very good story about how you do business.

events.text: {npc} has been expecting a better price, and says so. You can both hear how it sounds. {He} has a family and {he} has a position, and {he} has been told what will happen when the plot succeeds, and {he} would like you to understand that this is only a matter of good business. There is a fly on the rim of {his} cup. Neither of you looks at it.

choices.text: Say that is why you came

effects.log: You shake on it. {His} hand is very dry. You wash yours, later, and you are not sure why.

choices.text: Say good business has good memories

effects.log: {He} looks at you properly for the first time. {He} takes the silver. That is all you will ever have from {him}, and you will be counting it.

events.text: You know where it will be. You know the day, you know how many, and you know what they plan to tell people afterward. All they need is for you to come out alone, and so you send {npc} a very friendly note accepting the invitation. It is the first time you have looked forward to anything in years. You have a new coat made.

choices.text: Send the note

effects.log: It goes off, with a small gift. You sit down that evening to put your affairs in order, and then you go through what they know about you, and you begin to change it.

choices.text: Think again: wait a little longer

effects.log: You put the note away in a drawer. There is plenty of time, and they have not finished showing you how they work.

events.text: It is a lovely trap. You have come to feel quite warmly about it. Nobody has ever gone to so much trouble over you. A hall, a date, a pretext, an old friend to ask you there, and {npc} to make the speech. There are only two weaknesses in the whole thing: that they think you do not know, and that you are you.

choices.text: Say yes to the old friend

effects.log: You say yes, and they are visibly relieved. You feel almost sorry for them. It passes.

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. A thing like this can only be done once, and you would like to know more first.

events.text: Every one of your people has told you not to go. They are right. You have told them why you are going all the same, and they did not like that either. {npc} has been told, by people who think that they are betraying you, that you are tired, that you are careless, and that you will come alone. Only one of those things is true.

choices.text: Go

effects.log: You tell your people what to do if you are wrong, and then you do not think about it again. You sleep very well.

choices.text: Listen to them, for now

effects.log: You listen to them. They are very relieved. {npc} goes on waiting, and you go on watching {him} wait.

events.text: The next meeting of those who plotted against you is held in a back room at Kaifeng, and nobody comes. There were so many of them, once. You know this because you are sitting in the room. You have ordered enough for all of them, and it is very good, and after a while you eat it. It is a strange way to win anything.

choices.text: Pay the bill, and leave a note for the owner

effects.log: You pay for all of them. The owner gets a note to say the party will not be needing the room again. That will get around, in time.

choices.text: Leave it unpaid, in their names

effects.log: You sign the bill with each of their names, in a good hand. That gets around a good deal faster.

events.text: It ended without your ever seeing the end of it. One is gone, another has been bought, someone else has stopped answering letters. You had been braced for so many years that it takes a whole winter to notice that nothing has happened lately. You come across their last letter by accident, and it only says, in a tired hand, that perhaps it is time to let it drop.

choices.text: Keep the letter

effects.log: You keep it, in with the things you keep. Every so often you read it. It is the kindest thing any of them ever said to you.

choices.text: Burn it, and sleep

effects.log: You burn it, and go to bed. You sleep for two days, and when you wake up it is spring.

events.text: You had thought it was a funeral. The whole of the valley is here, in white. It is only when the doors close that you see who else is: {hnt_names}, and {npc} coming forward to read out your crimes, every one of them with a witness. The bier they have carried here, at the front of the hall, is empty, and it is about your size. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Stand up, and answer it

effects.log: You get up. You have never needed anybody's leave for that.

choices.text: Let the seal go, in front of all of them

effects.log: They built all this for someone two rungs lower. You watch them begin to count again.

choices.text: Light the signal: call on the houses

effects.log: You have been paying for this for years. Somewhere across the valley, a smoke goes up.

choices.text: Go out through the roof, and do not stop

effects.log: You go. It is not at all how you pictured it, and you do not stop for a very long time.

events.text: A friend you have known for thirty years has asked you to help with a small matter at the old salt-works, and comes along to show you the way. It is a beautiful evening. At the last gate your friend stops walking, and cannot look at you, and there is {npc}, and there are the others too: {hnt_names}. Your friend starts crying. Nobody else does. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Tell your friend to stand somewhere safe, and begin

effects.log: You do say it. You would not have thought so. Then you begin.

choices.text: Take your seal off, here, at this gate

effects.log: You say that you are sorry they did not ask. Nobody in the place can breathe.

choices.text: Tell them they should have counted your friends

effects.log: And then you wait, and it does not take long: there are torches on the ridge, carrying the colours of a house that owes you.

choices.text: Knock down the gate and run for it

effects.log: You are through it and away, and your friend is left standing in the road, and that is that.

events.text: Everyone is at the Mid-Autumn gathering on the lake, and you are a guest of honour, out on the island, on a boat that now has no oars. {npc} raises a cup to you from across the water. You count the other boats, and the people in them: {hnt_names}. It is very well lit. They have brought an audience, and hired a poet. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Stand up in the boat, and walk across

effects.log: You have done harder things than that. It will be something for the poet to get down.

choices.text: Let them see what they have in the boat

effects.log: The water goes flat in a ring, with you in the middle of it, and then the lanterns start to go out one at a time.

choices.text: Raise your cup back, and wait

effects.log: From behind the island come the boats of a house that owes you, a little late, and rowing hard.

choices.text: Go over the side, and swim for the far shore

effects.log: You leave your good boots and your name in the lake. Nobody ever does get the poem right.

events.text: The whole house has been called into the great hall, for a reading of the charges. You are on the floor, in front of the seat of judgment, and every door has someone at it. Beside the head stands {npc}. Along the wall: {hnt_names}. Somebody has been very thorough. Every elder has already been spoken to. It only remains for you to kneel. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Do not kneel

effects.log: You stay on your feet. Everyone sees it. That is a very loud thing to do in that room.

choices.text: Do not kneel, and let the seal go

effects.log: They had written that the accused would be two rungs lower. Someone starts to rub out the page.

choices.text: Say there are guests at the gate

effects.log: And there are. A house that owes you has sent more people than this hall can hold, and they would like to witness the proceedings.

choices.text: Take off the robe, and walk out

effects.log: You take off the robe and fold it. Nobody stops you, and they could. They have got what they came for.

events.text: You have been sent to inspect a mountain outpost, on the head's own orders, with twenty good people. All twenty are very quiet today. {npc} is waiting at the outpost. So are the others: {hnt_names}. The orders turn out to have come from someone else. They would like you to know that it will be recorded as an avalanche, and that it will be very sad. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Say they had better start the avalanche

effects.log: You have been in worse places than this. You cannot actually think when, but you must have been.

choices.text: Let the seal go, and let the mountain feel it

effects.log: Snow begins to come down from the ridge, and it has nothing to do with them. Those twenty good people drop their swords.

choices.text: Tell them who you left word with

effects.log: There are torches on the far pass. A house that owes you has been following you for three days, and it has been a very long three days.

choices.text: Go straight down the cliff

effects.log: It is not as bad as it looks. It is quite bad. They will write it down as an avalanche anyway.

events.text: A banquet for your promotion, and you ought to have known. They have set your place at the head table for the first time in your life. {npc} rises, cup in hand, to say a few words about how long you have been among them, and it goes on, and it is not a toast, and one by one down the table they stand up: {hnt_names}. The doors have been barred from outside. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Put down your cup, and stand up too

effects.log: You are the last one standing up, and you have the longest reach.

choices.text: Let the cup go, and everything with it

effects.log: Your cup breaks, and then every other cup in the hall. Then they understand what it is they have barred themselves in with.

choices.text: Knock three times on the table

effects.log: From outside, three knocks answer you. The doors come off. A house that owes you has been waiting in the yard all this time, in the cold.

choices.text: Go through the window

effects.log: It is an old window, and you take most of it with you, and you do not look back at the head table.

events.text: Those you lead have been called together for the anniversary of your founding, and you have come in to make the speech. You stop halfway through it. The front row is wrong. {npc} is sitting there, where nobody invited {him}, with your oldest people on either side of {him}, and behind them are the others: {hnt_names}. No one is looking at you. Then they all do. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Finish the speech, and then begin

effects.log: You finish it, to the last word, and you make them sit through all of it. It is a good speech.

choices.text: Stop speaking, and let the seal go

effects.log: Nobody here ever knew what they were following. Now they can feel it in their teeth. The front row is trying to stand and finding that it cannot.

choices.text: Look over their heads, at the doors

effects.log: Everyone turns. A house that owes you has come for the anniversary, and they have brought a very large gift.

choices.text: Set down the speech, and walk out through them

effects.log: They make way for you. It is so much worse than if they had not. You walk straight out through everything you made.

events.text: There is a letter from your oldest elder, asking you to come at once to the hall of tablets, alone, on a matter too serious to write down. You come at once. It is cold in there. Your elder is sitting among the tablets with their hands tied, looking at the floor, and {npc} sits by them, with a very sharp small knife, and the others are at the doors: {hnt_names}. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Say that they should untie the old one first

effects.log: You say it quietly. You have never yet asked anybody twice. Then you begin.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the seal go

effects.log: The tablets start to shake on their shelves. The knife in that very steady hand starts to shake as well.

choices.text: Say you did not come alone

effects.log: A long way off, you hear a door broken in, and then a nearer one. A house that owes you has got a very good sense of timing.

choices.text: Give them what they want, and leave

effects.log: You lay down the seal among the tablets. They untie the old one. You go out past them all, and it is very cold.

events.text: The great audience, at the New Year. Everyone is here, in full robes, and you are on the dais when the Grand Secretary comes forward with a memorial you have not read. Behind him comes {npc}, and behind {him}, one at a time, each with their following: {hnt_names}. It is entirely legal. It is the most legal thing you have ever seen. The guards are looking straight ahead. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Rise, and take the memorial yourself

effects.log: You have never come down those steps before. It is very quiet in the hall, and you can hear each one.

choices.text: Rise, and let the seal go, here on the dais

effects.log: Eight hundred officials go down flat, without having decided to. It was not a thing they could decide.

choices.text: Say that there is someone at the gate

effects.log: The sound reaches the hall first: drums, in the colours of a house that owes you, and coming up the great avenue with the whole city watching.

choices.text: Rise, and leave by the back of the dais

effects.log: There has always been a little door. Everyone who has ever sat there has checked. You go through it, and you do not hurry.

events.text: You have gone out to the summer palace, as you do each year, with the small household. It is on the fourth day that you realise you have not seen a courier. On the fifth the gardeners are soldiers. On the sixth {npc} comes up the walk with a very respectful bow, and the others behind: {hnt_names}. It is only for your own safety. The capital has been told that you are unwell. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Say that you feel very well, and walk toward the capital

effects.log: They will have to stop you with their hands. You would like to see who does that first.

choices.text: Say that you feel very well, and let it be seen

effects.log: It goes out from you in a slow ring, and every carp in the lake comes up to the surface. The gardeners put down their spades.

choices.text: Ask {him} to look up at the hills

effects.log: There are banners on the hills. A house that owes you heard about the couriers before you did.

choices.text: Get out over the garden wall tonight

effects.log: It has been a long time since you have climbed anything. It comes back to you, all of it, along with who you used to be.

events.text: Your own physician looks up from your wrist and then cannot look at you again. Somebody has been at your food for a year, a very little at a time. You have about a month, he thinks, unless you do what he has been told to tell you to do. {npc} is outside. So are the others: {hnt_names}. They have brought a very nice edict for you to sign, and they have left the date blank. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Have them in, and say that you would like to discuss the date

effects.log: You receive them sitting up. It takes a lot of doing. Nobody in that room has ever been so afraid of a sick person.

choices.text: Have them in, and stand up

effects.log: You were never poisoned by what they think you were. It takes a year of qi to burn all that out, and you do it in one breath, in front of them.

choices.text: Say you sent for someone a week ago

effects.log: And there they are, on the stairs: the head physician of a house that owes you, carrying a box, and with a hundred people behind her.

choices.text: Sign it, and go

effects.log: You sign it. They give you a month to get out of the city and a very good carriage. You have no idea why you feel so light.

events.text: It is over before the lamps need trimming. They are on the floor, or at the walls, or running, and it was so many years of work. {npc} is sitting against a pillar with one leg out in front of {him}, and {he} looks more interested than afraid. "I did tell them," {he} says. "I told them it would take more than this." Everybody is looking at you, to see what you do.

choices.text: Finish it

effects.log: You finish it, and nobody who saw it will ever try this again. That was the idea. It is a very quiet walk home.

choices.text: Let {him} live, and let everyone see it

effects.log: You turn your back on {him}. That is the worst thing anyone has ever done to {him}, and {he} knows it, and {he} will have many years to think about it.

events.text: You find that you are not even breathing hard. The last of them put down their swords a little while ago. {npc} has not, quite, but it is shaking, and {he} has stopped pretending otherwise. Someone at the back has started to read out a very different list of names, in a loud voice, to show which side they have been on all along.

choices.text: Tell them to stop reading, and take {npc} away for good

effects.log: You do not need to do it yourself. They are all so eager. It is over by the morning, and you make yourself watch.

choices.text: Take the sword out of {his} hand, and give it back to {him}

effects.log: You put it back in {his} hand and close {his} fingers on it. Then you leave. Nobody has ever seen a person so thoroughly beaten.

events.text: They said it could not be done. You had thought so too, for a while, about halfway through. Now the ones who are left are all kneeling, and they are very sorry, and {npc} is being held up by two of them. {He} spits. It was a good plot, and you tell {him} so. You find you mean it. There will not be another one like it.

choices.text: Thank {him} for the compliment, and end it

effects.log: It was a good plot. You will think about it often. There will be nobody left to discuss it with.

choices.text: Take down the whole of it from {him}, and let {him} go

effects.log: You make {him} tell you all of it, with a clerk, for three days. Then you open the door. It is a very useful document.

events.text: The sun is coming up. You had not noticed. Someone has given you a cup of something and you are holding it. They are bringing {npc} over to you, between two others, and {he} looks very old all of a sudden, and you try to remember how long you have known {him}. The people around you are waiting for you to say something that they can tell their children.

choices.text: Say "that is enough," and have it done

effects.log: You say it. That is what they will tell their children. You drink what is in the cup.

choices.text: Say "get {him} a chair"

effects.log: They get {him} a chair. It is not at all what they wanted to tell their children. You sit down beside {him} and watch the sun come up.

events.text: There is an odd silence, the kind you only get after a very large thing has stopped. {npc} has been waiting for you to look at {him}. "So," {he} says. "It really was only ever you, was it? We should have just asked you what you wanted, all those years ago." You try to remember whether anyone ever did. It occurs to you that someone did, in fact. You remember how you answered.

choices.text: Give {him} the same answer

effects.log: You give {him} the same answer, in the same words, and then you finish it.

choices.text: Tell {him} you have no idea what you wanted

effects.log: You tell {him} that, and for a moment you both almost laugh. Then you go. {He} is still sitting there when the others come for {him}.

events.text: It is not that you were weak. There were just too many, for too long, and they knew about the shoulder. You are on one knee. {npc} has come to look at you. "You will live," {he} says. "We had quite a discussion about that. It seems that it is much more useful to have everyone see you." They have already sent for your account books.

choices.text: Get up, and walk out in front of them

effects.log: You get up. It takes a while, and nobody helps. It is the last thing you own that they have not got a list for, and you walk out with it.

choices.text: Be gone by nightfall, to somewhere they cannot follow

effects.log: You get out while they are still counting. There is nothing left behind you that is worth going back for, for now.

choices.text: Stand and fight to the very last

ok.log: You do not know how you are still on your feet. Neither do they. They break all at once, the way a dam does, and it is {npc} who runs first.

fail.log: You make them pay for every step of it, and it is not enough. They will speak of it for a long time, very quietly.
fail.deathCause: the last stand at the trap

events.text: They will not even kill you. A clerk is reading out, in a flat voice, what you did, and what you never did, in one list, and nobody here can tell the difference, and by the end of the month nobody anywhere will. {npc} is looking at you with something like sympathy. You can no longer feel your right hand. They are taking the sign down off your name.

choices.text: Listen to the end

effects.log: You listen to it, every word. You would like to have it right, for later. You are going to want every line of it.

choices.text: Go, while they are still reading

effects.log: You go out quietly through the side, past a very embarrassed guard. They are still reading when you reach the river.

events.text: The verdict is read in full. They take the badge from your belt and break it on a stone in the yard, and it is an old custom, and it takes three tries. {npc} stands with the elders. People you taught are standing at the wall with their eyes down. There is a gate, and there is a road beyond it. Nobody has told you what happens if you do not go through it. You find you already know.

choices.text: Go through the gate with your head up

effects.log: It is a long yard. You look at each of them on the way out, and every one remembers it. Then you are on the road, with no banner at all.

choices.text: Do not wait for the verdict to finish

effects.log: You are over the wall before the second try on the badge. It is one more thing they can read out. You have got some years of walking to do.

choices.text: Stand and fight to the very last

ok.log: The stone in the yard cracks before you do. The elders are the first ones to run, and it is a very long time before anyone in that house uses the word verdict again.

fail.log: You take a great many of them down with you, and it is not enough. The yard needs a new stone.
fail.deathCause: the last stand in the yard

events.text: You had always wondered who would take your seat when you fell. It turns out to be someone quite small, who has already had the room measured. {npc} shakes {his} hand warmly. You are told that you may take your personal things. They have been very carefully packed in advance, and someone has gone through them all, and left you the ones that they did not want.

choices.text: Take the box

effects.log: You carry it out yourself. There is a very old teapot in it, and you are surprised to find you are glad of that. You are nobody now. It is quite something.

choices.text: Leave the box, and go tonight

effects.log: You leave it all on the step. By morning you are a long way from anyone who might ask how you are.

events.text: They do not take what you built. They are much too clever for that. {npc} only stands up in the middle of it, and invites those who have doubts to come and stand with {him}, and you watch your own people walk across the floor, one by one, and they look at you, each one, and then they do it. Your name is still over the gate. It will be, for as long as you like.

choices.text: Stand where you are, until the last has crossed
