effects.log: You stay, and you count them. Those left on your side of the floor do not make a very large number, and you learn every one of their names again.

choices.text: Hand the keys to the oldest, and go away for a while

effects.log: You put them in those old hands and you go, by the road you first came in on. They can run it. You made sure of that. You wish that you had made less sure.

choices.text: Stand and fight to the very last

ok.log: You go across the floor yourself, to {npc}, with everybody watching. When it is over, the ones who crossed start to cross back. They do it very slowly, and they do not look up.

fail.log: You go across the floor to {him}, and you do not get all the way. It is what they will tell.
fail.deathCause: the last stand in your own hall

events.text: It has all been done according to your own rules. You wrote them well, and it took {npc} years to learn them, and {he} has walked through every one of them in order, and now you are head of a house with an empty treasury, half its people and a very long list of apologies that you have to make. They leave you the chair. You can see that it was the cruellest thing they could think of.

choices.text: Sit in it, and begin again

effects.log: You sit. It is a very hard chair. In the morning you start writing the apologies, and you get through nine of them before lunch.

choices.text: Leave it empty for a while, and go

effects.log: You leave it. Someone will dust it. You have not been out on the road alone since you were young, and you find you still know how.

events.text: They do not depose you. They are very careful about that. They only bring you the edicts, already written, and you sign them, and the Grand Secretary thanks you, and {npc} has been given a very good title. All of your people have been promoted to places a long way away. There is a great deal of ceremony. You are the most honoured prisoner in the history of the Empire.

choices.text: Sign, and watch them, and remember

effects.log: You sign. You have very good handwriting, and you have a very good memory, and nobody has thought to take away either of those. You are in no hurry at all.

choices.text: Leave it all to them, and go to the far mountains to pray

effects.log: A pious ruler goes off to pray, for ten years. It is all perfectly in order. Nobody at all believes it, and it is a great relief to everyone.

choices.text: Stand and fight to the very last

ok.log: You rise from the dais and walk toward {npc}, and the guards find that they cannot, and by the time you reach {him} the edicts are burning. It will be spoken of for a thousand years.

fail.log: The guards remember themselves in time. {npc} makes a very fine speech about it.
fail.deathCause: the last stand in the palace

events.text: You still sit in the chair. All the provinces still send you tribute, and it arrives in smaller carts. All your ministers kneel, and they wait until you have finished, and they go off to do something else. {npc} has been kind enough to take on the burden of your correspondence. It is a very curious thing to be an Emperor of the room you happen to be sitting in.

choices.text: Learn the room

effects.log: You learn the room. There are eleven people in it you can trust and one that you can use. It will do to start with.

choices.text: Announce a long pilgrimage

effects.log: You take a small household and a very long list of temples. The capital sees you off with a touching display of grief.

events.text: There is a boat at the end of the salt marsh, and it is not one of theirs. You have kept that boat, paid up, for twenty years, without quite telling yourself why. By the time the sun is up the coast has gone flat and blue behind you. {npc} will be telling everyone you ran. That is true. There is an island that you know of where they have never heard of anyone. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Go to the island

effects.log: Nobody there has heard of you. You mend nets for a while, very badly. You have ten years, you think. It seems about right.

choices.text: Go on past it, as far as the boat will go

effects.log: You go on past it. There is a great deal of sea, and it does not have any opinion of you at all.

events.text: You cross the western pass in the last week before the snow closes it, with a mule, and a good coat, and a name you have just made up. Behind you, down in all that country you know so well, {npc} is having a very good winter. You look back once. You had told yourself that you would not. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Keep the mule, and keep walking

effects.log: It is a very good mule. In time, you will learn the names of all of the mountains out here, and nobody will ever learn yours.

choices.text: Find a monastery that does not ask

effects.log: They give you a broom. It is ten years before anyone there asks you anything, and then it is only about the broom.

events.text: A friend you had forgotten you had sends a cart for you, by night, with no lamp. They take you through three checkpoints in a load of cabbages. You lie there among them, the strongest fighter in the central plains, or whatever you are now, and listen to {npc}'s people going through the cart ahead. The cabbages are very cold. You could stop this at any moment. You do not. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Stay in the cabbages

effects.log: You stay. It is the longest night of your life, and the funniest, some years later. You are out of the country by morning.

choices.text: Thank the driver, and walk the last part alone

effects.log: You give all that you have left to the driver, and then you walk. It feels better, and it is much colder.

events.text: They have left the north gate open for you. {npc} has made sure of it, and {he} is sitting on a stool beside it, with a pot of tea, in case you wanted to say something. You stop, because you would rather not have them say you hurried. {He} pours for you. Neither of you says very much. "Ten years," {he} says. "Say ten years. After that I will be old, and I will not mind so much." {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Drink the tea

effects.log: You finish it. It is very good tea. You give {him} back the cup, and you walk out of the gate. You will remember the ten years, and so will {he}.

choices.text: Leave the tea, and walk through

effects.log: You walk past the stool, and you do not look at the cup. {He} goes on sitting there. Behind you, you can hear {him} pour it out on the ground.

events.text: Ten years, and the road home is shorter than you remember. The ferryman is a different ferryman. You have a beard, or you do not, and nobody looks twice. You sit in the teahouse and listen to what they say about {hnt_lead}, and what they say about you, and it turns out that the second is a very old story now, and not told very well.

choices.text: Go and see {hnt_lead}

effects.log: You make no secret of it. {hnt_lead} comes out on the steps to meet you, and is old, and has been waiting. It does not take long, and then everyone knows you are back.

choices.text: Let them have it, and sit a while longer

effects.log: You finish your tea. It is a poor story, and it no longer has much to do with you. You find that is quite restful.

events.text: You come home over the same pass, in the first week of the thaw. There are children on the road who have never heard of you. You go into the market and buy a bowl of noodles, and you eat them standing up, and it is only when you come to pay that the old woman looks up. She looks for a while. She takes your coin. "They said you would be taller," she says.

choices.text: Ask her where {hnt_lead} lives now

effects.log: She tells you. It is a very nice house. You get there by evening, and you sit down on the step, and you wait to be noticed.

choices.text: Ask her if she needs anything carried

effects.log: She does, in fact. It turns out there is a good deal to be done around here, and most of it has nothing at all to do with anyone who ever plotted anything.

events.text: A letter finds you, at the far end of everything, in the tenth year: "Time's up." There is no signature, and it is in a hand you know very well. You turn it over, for a long time, in a place where nobody can read. {hnt_lead} has had all of ten years to get ready. So have you. It is a very good thing for both of you to have had something to do.

choices.text: Go back, and keep the appointment

effects.log: You go back and keep it. It is everything that either of you had hoped for. The jianghu talks about nothing else for a year.

choices.text: Write back, and stay where you are

effects.log: You write two words, and you send it. You have a garden here now. You will never know how that letter was received, and you will think about it a lot.

events.text: It has been a long time since they took everything. You have got most of it back, or else you have stopped wanting it. Then this spring you hear that {hnt_lead} is holding a great birthday feast, with all of the old names at the table, and has been heard to say that you were never really a threat at all. You still have your memory. It is the one thing that nobody took.

choices.text: Go to the feast

effects.log: You walk in during the third toast. Nobody has ever heard a room go that quiet. You drink {hnt_lead}'s health, by name, and you tell them all the true story, and then you leave.

choices.text: Send a very small gift, with no name on it

effects.log: You send a little jar of cheap tea, the kind that you drank together, back then. It should be just enough to spoil the meal. It is all you need, now.

events.text: Someone has come to you, one of the young ones who used to stand at the wall with their eyes down, and who is not so young now. They have the papers. All of them. They have been keeping them for years, in a jar, under a floor. They think it is time that it all came out. They put the jar down on your table, and they look very tired. {hnt_lead} is still very well thought of.

choices.text: Open the jar

effects.log: You read it all. Then you take it out to all of the places where it would do the most harm, one after the other, and you do not raise your voice once. It takes a year, and {hnt_lead} does not get through it.

choices.text: Thank them, and bury the jar again

effects.log: You thank them. You give them something to eat. You put it back where it was. You had thought that this would be harder.

events.text: You have been walking for a while, and without really deciding to, you find yourself at the gate of {hnt_lead}. It is evening. You could go in. You have got back quite a lot of what you used to be, and there is nobody here who could stop you. Inside, somebody is singing to a child, rather badly. You stand there for quite a long time.

choices.text: Knock

effects.log: You knock. It is a very short conversation, on the step, and nobody there will ever forget it. You go home a good deal lighter.

choices.text: Go home

effects.log: You go home. It is a lovely evening, and you have got the whole of the road to yourself.

events.text: You had thought it might be one of the others. It is {npc}, who you taught to hold a blade, standing with them at the end, with your own third form in {his} hands. {He} is the only one there who does not look afraid of you. You have seen that look before, you think: on your own face, the day you first thought that you might be better than anyone had told you.

choices.text: Ask {him} why

effects.log: {He} tells you. It is all true, as far as it goes. It takes you years to be able to think about it, and you still get the third form wrong now, sometimes.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let {him} go

effects.log: You say nothing. {He} stands there a moment longer, and {he} goes. You have taught a great many people, and you do not talk about this one.

events.text: Among the letters that they left behind, you find a long one from {npc}, in that careful handwriting you corrected for so many years. It has your schedule in it, and the way you sleep, and how you take your tea. It is very accurate. It is, in fact, an excellent piece of work. You taught {him} to be thorough, and you are looking for someone to be angry at.

choices.text: Keep the letter

effects.log: You put it away with the first exercise {he} ever gave you. They are in the same hand. You do not really know why you need to know that.

choices.text: Correct it, and send it back

effects.log: You find two mistakes in it. You mark them, in red, the way you always did, and you send it back to wherever {he} has gone. There is no answer.

events.text: There is an empty room in your house now. You have not had it cleared. {npc} left a coat behind, and some notes on a form that {he} never got right, and a very old pair of practice shoes. Those who are still with you walk past that door a little quickly. You won, they all say, and everybody is very glad. Nobody has said which part of that you are supposed to feel.

choices.text: Have the room cleared

effects.log: You have it cleared and painted, and you give it to the next person who comes. They ask who had it before, and you tell them someone who could not get the form right.

choices.text: Keep the door shut

effects.log: You keep the door shut. Now and then you go in and look at the notes. {He} was very nearly right about that form, and you wish you had told {him}.

events.text: Your people have asked you to come and open the new hall they built in your name, and it is a handsome thing. The doors are very thick. You notice that when they close. {npc} steps out from behind the great painted screen with the others behind {him}: {hnt_names}. Nobody you brought here has moved to help, because they are all looking at the floor. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Ask which of them chose the screen

effects.log: It is a good screen. You will be sorry to see what happens to it.

choices.text: Let the seal go, in the hall that bears your name

effects.log: The new roof beams begin to tick, one after another. Everyone in the place looks up, and then at you.

choices.text: Say the hall has another door

effects.log: It does. You paid for the plans. A house that owes you has been standing behind it for an hour, with some impatience.

choices.text: Leave it to them, and walk out by the kitchens

effects.log: The cooks do not look up as you go by. They have a great many people to feed tonight, and none of it is your concern now.

events.text: A letter from a branch of your people: they have been attacked, and they beg you to come at once, with only those you can trust. You bring eleven. At the river crossing there is nobody attacked at all, only {npc}, sitting on an upturned boat and looking at you with something like pity, and behind {him} on the bank: {hnt_names}. The eleven have stopped walking. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Ask the eleven to stand aside

effects.log: Some of them do. You do not look to see which. There will be time for that afterward, if there is an afterward.

choices.text: Let go of the seal, here on the bank

effects.log: The river stands still for about a breath. Nobody who saw that will ever be quite sure what they saw, and all of them believe it.

choices.text: Look across the water

effects.log: Boats, a long line of them, flying the colours of a house that owes you. You told nobody. That is why they are here.

choices.text: Get into the river, and let it take you

effects.log: It is cold and it is fast and it does not care who founded what. You come ashore a long way down, with nothing that has your name on it.

events.text: Everyone has come for the naming of your heir. It is the happiest day your house has had in years. The cup comes to you, and it is {npc} who has carried it, with a very low bow, and you know by the smell, and you know that {he} knows you know. Behind {him}, in the seats of honour you gave them yourself: {hnt_names}. {He} goes on holding it out. Every eye is on your hand. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Take the cup, and pour it on the floor

effects.log: The floor begins to smoke a little. It is an old floor, and everyone can see it. That is all the speech you are going to need.

choices.text: Take the cup and drink it, and let them see what you are

effects.log: You drink it to the bottom. It should have done something. You set it down, and the seal goes with it, and now nobody in the seats of honour can stand.

choices.text: Hand it to the guest from the house that owes you

effects.log: That guest sniffs it, and smiles, and a good many people in the back of the hall take off their outer robes. They were not dressed for a naming.

choices.text: Set it down untasted, and go, before the children see

effects.log: You make some small excuse and you go out past the children. They wave at you. It is what you will remember.

events.text: The rains have broken the dyke above your lands, and you have gone up with everyone else to carry earth, in old clothes, in the dark. Hours later you notice that those around you have stopped carrying. It is {npc}, up on the bank, with a lantern. And the others: {hnt_names}. There is a lot of water behind that dyke. Your people are asleep below it. They have only to take out one more stake. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Keep carrying earth

effects.log: You pick up the next basket. You are not going to discuss it until that dyke is safe. Whatever they do next, they will do it in front of the people they have got up here to watch.

choices.text: Let the seal go, and hold the water

effects.log: It is the only time in your life that you have ever been truly glad of it. The water stops. Everyone on that bank can see what has stopped it.

choices.text: Blow the horn on your belt

effects.log: It carries a long way on a wet night. A house that owes you has been camped two valleys off, on some excuse, for a month.

choices.text: Give them what they want, if they leave the stake

effects.log: You put the seal down in the mud, and you say the words. They leave the stake. You walk down in the rain, past your own sleeping house.

events.text: You get a note in a child's hand, asking you to come to the old mill where someone you once saved is dying. It is true, as it happens: they are. They have been kept alive for it. {npc} is holding the cup for them, very gently. And in the dark among the grindstones you can make out the rest: {hnt_names}. The one on the bed opens their eyes, and says your name, and says that they are sorry. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Sit with them first

effects.log: It takes about an hour. Nobody stops you. When you stand up you have been told everything, and you are not in a hurry at all.

choices.text: Close their eyes, and let go of the seal

effects.log: The grindstones begin to turn, by themselves, with no water in the race. All of them can hear that.

choices.text: Say that the miller works for someone else now

effects.log: The doors are opened from outside. The house that owes you bought this mill a year ago, and you are a little surprised yourself.

choices.text: Go out by the race, and do not look back at the bed

effects.log: You go. You will be asked about that, later, by the only person who has any right to, and it will not be anyone here.

events.text: The Ten Greatest are to sit down together in public at Mount Tai, for the first time in a generation, and you have been asked to join them. Nobody has ever been so polite. You are halfway up the thousand steps when you see that there is nobody behind you and nobody coming down. {npc} is waiting at the next turn, on a folding stool. Above {him}, in the mist: {hnt_names}. It is a very long way down. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Go on up, one step at a time

effects.log: They could have done this anywhere, and they chose the steps. You take that as a compliment. You go on climbing, at the pace you started with.

choices.text: Stop climbing, and let the mountain feel it

effects.log: The mist goes back from you in a ring, all the way to the top. Up there, somebody drops a sword, and you can hear it going down the steps for a long time.

choices.text: Sit down on a step, and wait

effects.log: You wait about as long as it takes to eat something. Then there are banners on the path below, and on the one above, in the colours of a house that owes you.

choices.text: Go over the edge, into the mist

effects.log: It is not a good idea. It is the only one left. They will be finding pieces of your coat in those trees for years.

events.text: A mission has come down: an escort, four carts, nothing at all, and you are to lead it in person. On the third day you open one of the carts, out of boredom. It is full of the banners of an enemy house, and letters in your hand, and by the time you have shut it {npc} is riding up the road, with a magistrate, and the elders of your own hall, and the rest: {hnt_names}. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Open every cart for them

effects.log: You throw the covers back yourself, all four, and you stand up on the first one. You would like everyone to get a good look at the handwriting.

choices.text: Get down off the cart, and let them see what they caught

effects.log: The horses go down on their knees first. The magistrate takes a little longer. Your own elders know that feeling, or think they do. They have never felt this.

choices.text: Ask whose those riders are on the ridge

effects.log: A house that owes you has been following this nothing at all for three days, and it has some questions about those letters.

choices.text: Cut a horse loose, and go

effects.log: You go, and they have the carts. That is what the story is going to be. You will have a long time to think about how good it was.

events.text: You come back from a long errand to find your room just as you left it. All of your things have been moved, very slightly, to the left. In the corridor they bow, and go on bowing. At the end of it the door of the great hall stands open for you, and it is the only door that does. {npc} is on the far side. So are all the rest: {hnt_names}. A chair stands in the middle of the floor. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Sit down in the chair

effects.log: You sit, and you cross your legs, and you ask them what they would like to know. It is not what any of them rehearsed.

choices.text: Stand behind the chair, and let them feel it

effects.log: You put a hand on its back and the chair comes apart under your fingers. You had not meant to do that. You find you do not mind.

choices.text: Ask if they would mind one more guest

effects.log: The guest has come a long way. A house that owes you does not usually send its own head on these occasions, and you can see that it is having an effect.

choices.text: Turn round, and go back down the corridor

effects.log: It is very quiet. You go by all the people bowing. Not one of them straightens up until you have gone.

events.text: The tomb of your ancestors, for the great spring sacrifice, and the rule is that you go down alone. It has been the rule for four hundred years, and you can see now how useful that has been to somebody. There is someone already there in the third chamber, on the steps, with a lamp: it is {npc}. There are others behind {him}: {hnt_names}. The door above you has made a noise. It is a heavy door. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Make the offerings first

effects.log: You go on with it, every bow, every cup, in the proper order, with them looking on. You are in no hurry. They are, after all, your own dead.

choices.text: Put down the cup, and let the ancestors feel it

effects.log: Every lamp in the third chamber leans toward you, all at once, against what wind there is. Nobody down here is a very religious person. Some of them are now.

choices.text: Say the rule was changed last year

effects.log: And it was, in a small edict that no one read. The door above opens again. There are a great many feet on the stairs, of a house that owes you.

choices.text: Take the old way out, that only you were told

effects.log: Every ruler is told about it, and every ruler laughs. It is a very tight fit, and a very long crawl, and you come out in a turnip field, in your robes of state.

events.text: At the great review you are on the high stand, with three hundred thousand spears drawn up below you. It has been arranged that they will all salute at the third drum. You have stood here a dozen times before. The second drum goes, and {npc} comes up the steps with the others behind {him}: {hnt_names}. {He} says in your ear, very respectfully, that it depends on which way they turn at the third. {hnt_stake}

choices.text: Tell {him} to have them beat the third drum

effects.log: You say it loud enough to be heard on the stand. Then you turn your back on {him}, and you look down at all of those spears. You have been looking at them for a long time.

choices.text: Step to the rail, and let them feel who is up here

effects.log: It goes out across the field like wind across barley, and three hundred thousand men find that they are kneeling. Nobody has beaten any drum.

choices.text: Ask {him} to count the banners on the left

effects.log: There are rather more of them than there should be, in the colours of a house that owes you. {He} counts them. {He} loses count.

choices.text: Go down by the back of the stand

effects.log: There is a horse there. Someone left it there for you, and you will never find out who. Behind you, the third drum sounds, to an empty stand.

events.text: They have been very fair. There was a hearing, in front of all the sects, with your name and all your deeds in order, and every word of it was very nearly true. {npc} spoke last, with real sorrow. Afterward a boy who used to carry your bags comes up to you, and takes off his hat, and asks you if he can have the bags, since you will not be needing anyone to carry them.

choices.text: Give him the bags

effects.log: You give him the bags. He thanks you. He is a good boy, and there is nothing in them. You walk on, with your hands empty, and find you can swing your arms.

choices.text: Tell him you will carry them yourself, a long way from here

effects.log: You carry them yourself, and it is a long way. You had forgotten how much you owned that you never looked at.

events.text: Your name is taken off the wall of those who have served. It takes a man with a chisel about an hour, and they have asked you to stay and watch, as is the custom. {npc} has brought a stool for you, and that is not the custom. You sit. A very young disciple is sweeping up the chips, and looking at them, and then at you, as if nobody had told that child anything about any of this.

choices.text: Stay until the chisel stops

effects.log: You stay to the end. You thank the man with the chisel. He has made a very clean job of it, and on the way out you take one of the chips.

choices.text: Get up, and go before it is done

effects.log: You do not stay for the last part of your name. You can hear it behind you as far as the gate.

events.text: You are given an accounting of your own house. {npc} has had it all drawn up, and {he} reads it to you in front of your people: who you favoured, what you spent, whom you promised and forgot. It is all true. There is no forgery in it anywhere. It is by a long way the worst thing they have done, and your own people are listening to it with their heads on one side.

choices.text: Hear it to the end, and ask for the copy

effects.log: You take the copy. You will go through it, line by line, with those who stay. There are not so many left, and they can all read.

choices.text: Leave the house to whoever wants it, for a while

effects.log: You go while {he} is still on the second page. The ones who were listening hear you go, and they do not look round.

events.text: Nobody could call it a coup. Your regulations have merely been reviewed. It has been found that the Emperor should not trouble with the provinces, or the army, or the salt, and {npc} has a new seal cut for all that. They have left you the calendar. You still have the sole right to announce the first day of spring, and the old court astronomer comes to see you about it, in tears.

choices.text: Announce the first day of spring, correctly, every year

effects.log: You give it your whole attention. It is the only true thing still done from this chair, and the farmers go by it. You get to know the astronomer quite well.

choices.text: Leave him the calendar, and go off to see the provinces yourself

effects.log: You go. They say that you have gone to pray. You stand in a good many fields, in plain clothes, and it is all a great deal bigger than the maps.

events.text: The first winter away. Nobody out here has any use for what you were. A woman who keeps goats asks if you are any good with a hammer, and you say no, and she gives you one. You have held every kind of weapon there is. By spring you can mend a fence that stays mended, and she has started paying you in cheese.

choices.text: Mend the rest of the fences

effects.log: There are a lot of them. It is a good thing to be bad at something again, and you get a little less bad at it.

choices.text: Move on before she asks your name

effects.log: You go before the thaw. She has had people like you through here before, and she leaves the hammer by the door anyway.

events.text: A trader comes through with news that is a year old. Your name comes up, in passing, in a list of what has changed in the central plains. It was just after the price of salt. He has it slightly wrong. He does not know who he is talking to, and offers to sell you a very good pair of boots. You had thought that you would mind a good deal more than this.

choices.text: Buy the boots

effects.log: They are a very good pair of boots. You ask him about the price of salt, and find that you are honestly interested.

choices.text: Ask him to tell you the rest of it

effects.log: He tells you all of it. You sit up late. It does you no good at all, and you ask the next trader as well.

events.text: There is a fight in the town where you have been wintering, over nothing, between people who cannot fight. One of them has a knife, and has picked it up by the wrong end. You could end this from where you are sitting, without putting down your bowl. You are nobody here. Nobody has ever been so restful as this nobody. The one with the knife is about seventeen.

choices.text: Put down your bowl

effects.log: It takes one hand and it is very gentle. Then the whole town is looking at you, in a way you know very well, and it is time to find a different town.

choices.text: Go on eating

effects.log: It ends badly, in the ordinary way, and you finish your soup. That is what it means, to be nobody. You think about it for some time.

events.text: You have started to practise again, out behind the sheepfolds, at dawn. Nobody is watching and nobody will ever know. It has been a long time since you did the forms for no reason. You find a mistake in the second one that you have been making for forty years and that all of your teachers made too. There is nobody in the world to tell about it.

choices.text: Fix it

effects.log: You fix it. It takes the whole summer. It is the best work that you have ever done, and only the sheep know.

choices.text: Write it down, and leave it at a temple

effects.log: You leave it with the monks, unsigned. It may be read in a hundred years. Somebody out there will have to work out who did this.

events.text: Somebody out here has heard a very good story. It is about you, as it happens. The teller is an old soldier at an inn, and he has you ten feet tall and always in the right. In his version, you were betrayed and you will come back on the day you are most needed. A whole table of herdsmen is listening. You have been sitting among them for an hour, and you are holding his cup for him.

choices.text: Buy him another

effects.log: You buy him another, and you ask what you did next. It is really very good. You would like to have met that person.

choices.text: Tell him it was not like that

effects.log: He looks you up and down, and he laughs until he has to put his head on the table. It is the best laugh you have had in years.

events.text: Someone has found you. It is a very young person with a very old sword, who has walked for two years to get here. They would like you to come back. They have got a speech. The people are suffering under {hnt_lead}, they say, and when you ask what people, they tell you, and they have all the names right. They have also got it all completely wrong, and they are looking at you as if the sun had come up.

choices.text: Teach them what you can, and send them home

effects.log: You give it a season. They go home with a much better grip and a much worse opinion of you, and that is about the right way round.

choices.text: Go back with them, before your time

effects.log: You had not known how much you had been waiting for somebody to ask. They talk the whole way there, and you start to work out what it is going to cost.

events.text: You fall ill out here, of something ordinary, in a hut. There is no pill for it within a thousand miles. A family who have never heard of you take it in turns to sit up with you, and they feed you broth with a horn spoon. All of your power does nothing. It is about two weeks. On the last night the smallest one asks if you will be able to help with the lambing.

choices.text: Help with the lambing

effects.log: You help with the lambing. You are not much use, and it is the middle of the night. It is possible that this is what the whole thing has been for.

choices.text: Leave them all your silver, and go in the night

effects.log: You leave what you have under the horn spoon. It is much more than they will ever know what to do with, and that is its own kind of trouble.

events.text: It is a very long way to anywhere. You have got into the habit of talking to the mule, or the sea, or whatever you have got. One evening you hear yourself, going through it for the hundredth time: what you should have said, who you should have watched, what you would do to each of them. You have got it word perfect. It occurs to you that you have not looked at the sky in about a year.

choices.text: Look at the sky

effects.log: It is a very good one. You had forgotten. You do not stop going through it all, but you do it a little less, and the heart goes quieter.

choices.text: Go on through it once more

effects.log: You go through it once more. You find a better way of putting the part about the seal. You are going to be very ready when the time comes.

events.text: It is nearly over. You have been counting, you find, for some time now, without having decided to. You have a place here. There are people who would notice if you stopped coming by. You have a bowl that is yours, and you know whose dog that is. A year or two, and you can go home. You look around at all of it, and at the road going east. You are less sure of that word than you were.

choices.text: Start saying your goodbyes, early

effects.log: It takes a long time, because you do it properly. Nobody here will ever know who it was that mended all those fences.

choices.text: Do not tell anyone yet

effects.log: You say nothing, and you go on as you were. You have left a great many places in your life, and you know how good it is to have one more ordinary day.

events.text: A rider comes out of the east, looking for you by name. Your real name. There is not much left of the old alliance, the letter says, and {hnt_lead} is getting old, and the ten years you were given have only a little way to run. You could be home by the thaw. The letter is not signed. It does not say what you ought to do, only that someone thought that you would want to know.

choices.text: Wait out your time, to the day

effects.log: You burn it, and you wait. You said ten, and you will do ten. Nobody will ever be able to say you could not keep to that.

choices.text: Saddle up, and go

effects.log: You leave that night. You have waited long enough for anybody. They will all know by the time you get there, and you find you would like them to.

events.text: You find a grey hair, or a stiff knee, or some other small thing that power is meant to spare you, and you sit and look at it for a long time. Ten years is nothing, you had told yourself. You have a great many more years than that. But these ten were real, and there were mornings in them. You start to wonder what you are going home to do, exactly, and whether it is what you left to do.

choices.text: Decide what you will do

effects.log: You work it out over a whole winter. It is not what you thought it would be, and it is a lot shorter than the list you used to go over with the mule.

choices.text: Leave it till you get there

effects.log: You leave it. You have found that things are generally clearer once you can see the walls.

events.text: A letter has reached you, from the people you left. It is very correct. It reports the harvest, the numbers, and two deaths, and a dispute about a well which they have settled in a way that you would never have thought of. It is a much better settlement than yours would have been. It ends by hoping that you are well. Nobody has asked what you think about any of it.

choices.text: Write back, about the well

effects.log: You write back to say that it was well done. It takes you four drafts to say only that. The next letter is a little warmer.

choices.text: Do not write

effects.log: You put it with the others. They will go on as they are, and you are in no position to say otherwise, and that was the whole point.

events.text: One of your oldest has come all this way, on bad knees, to bring you a thing that needed your own seal. It did not, really. You can both see that. You sit outside, and you have the seal stamped on a bit of nothing, and neither of you mentions the people who walked across the floor. They have kept your rooms just as they were, you are told. They have got rather dusty.

choices.text: Tell them to give the rooms to someone who needs them

effects.log: You see the old face try not to show what it thinks of that. It is a very long way back for those knees. They will be telling that one at home.

choices.text: Ask for all of the news

effects.log: You keep them up half the night. They know it all, and you had forgotten how much you liked hearing them tell it.

events.text: You hear about it from a horse trader: someone of your house has put up a very good school, a long way from any place you ever thought of. They teach your first form, with a small change. You go and look, from the far side of the road, in your old coat. A dozen children are doing it in the yard, badly. The change is an improvement. They have your name over the door, spelled wrong.

choices.text: Go in and show them the third step

effects.log: You are just an old traveller who seems to know something. They give you a meal. You come back through a few more times, in the years you have left out here.

choices.text: Stay on your side of the road

effects.log: You watch until they are called in for dinner. It is all still going on, and you have nothing to do with it. You find that this was what you came to see.

events.text: The official gazette reaches you, four months late. You have issued a very sensible edict on canal dredging. You are said to be in good health, and to be at your prayers. There is a list of honours you have been graciously pleased to bestow. You look through it for the names of the people who sent you here. They are all there, and you have been very generous.

choices.text: Read it to the end

effects.log: You read every word of it, by a sheep-fat lamp. It is rather a well-run empire. You make a few notes in the margin, out of habit.

choices.text: Use it to light the fire

effects.log: It burns well, which is more than can be said for most official paper. A herdsman asks if you have any more.

events.text: You are standing in a line, in a county town you have never seen, to pay a tax you once signed. It is quite a long line. The clerk is rude to the old man in front of you, about a stamp which you yourself introduced, in your second year, for reasons which seemed good at the time. When you get to the window, he is rude to you too. You have never in your whole life been so interested in anything.

choices.text: Pay it, and ask how the stamp works

effects.log: He tells you, and it is worse than you could have imagined. You make a note. There will be a very surprised clerk some day, if there is a some day.

choices.text: Help the old man with his form

effects.log: You help him. You have got very bad at forms. Between you, you get it wrong in a way the clerk has never seen, and he has to go and ask someone.

events.text: You know this smell. It took you years the first time. events.text: You had quite forgotten {hnt_fallen}. {npc} has not. {He} has found you at a roadside stall. {He} is young, and {he} has the same way of standing as the one you killed, and {he} has been practising something for a long time. "I am the {hnt_kin} of {hnt_fallen}," {he} says. {He} has rehearsed it. {His} voice shakes, once, on the name. There is a good deal of steel in the way {he} goes on standing there.

choices.text: Put down your bowl, and end it

ok.log: It is not a long fight. {He} was very good, for {his} age. There is nobody left to come after this one, and you finish your soup, because it is paid for.

fail.log: {He} was very good, and you were not expecting that. {He} leaves you bleeding by the stall, and {he} walks off to practise some more.

choices.text: Beat {him}, and leave {him} living

ok.log: You put {him} on the ground without hurting {him} much. {He} lies there looking at the sky. {He} will be back, you think, or {he} will find some others who want to come with {him}.

fail.log: {He} is better than you allowed for, and you were holding back. You are the one on the ground. {He} looks down at you for some time.

choices.text: Tell {him} what {hnt_fallen} did, and what you did

ok.log: You tell it all, the whole of it, and you spare nobody, least of all yourself. {He} stands there a long time. Then {he} puts up {his} sword, and {he} goes. {He} does not forgive you. {He} will just not be doing this.

fail.log: {He} hears you out, and it makes no difference. {He} says thank you for telling {him}, and {he} draws. You get out of it alive, and {he} has got some new things to hate you for.

events.text: There has been somebody following you for some months: not very well, and then, as the months go on, rather better. You turn round at last on the bridge at Longmen. It is {npc}. "{hnt_fallen} taught me to walk like that," {he} says, "and I was the {hnt_kin}, and I was in the next room." {He} is not much more than a grown child. {He} has got one of those very patient faces, and you have seen where they end up.

choices.text: Finish it on the bridge

ok.log: It is a good bridge. It has seen a lot of that. You look over the rail for a little while before you go on.

fail.log: {He} has learned a lot, following you. {He} knows the shoulder. You come off that bridge limping, and {he} is standing where you left {him}.

choices.text: Ask what {he} wants to know

ok.log: It is not what you expected. {He} wants to know if it was quick. You tell {him}. You walk the rest of the bridge together, not talking, and at the far end {he} turns off. You do not see {him} again.

fail.log: {He} wanted to know if it was quick, and you hesitate. {He} sees that. {He} will be following you again by spring, and this time you will not notice.

choices.text: Keep walking

effects.log: You turn around and keep walking. {He} goes on following. It is a long road, and there are others who would be very glad to walk it with {him}.

events.text: It was going so well. You have just had a report from one of your people, with all the usual names in it, and among them, in a very careful hand, is {npc}. You looked {him} in the eye. You let {him} walk out of it last time, or you paid {him} to. You remember what {he} said to you, and you even remember what the weather was doing. You find you are not so surprised as you ought to be, and that is the worst of it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let {him} think you do not know

effects.log: You say nothing. You send {him} the usual gift at the New Year. It will be something to have up your sleeve, when the day comes.

choices.text: Send {him} back what you gave

effects.log: You have it delivered, with a note: the date, and nothing else. {He} will show it to the others. They will all know now that you know. You find that you want them to.

events.text: {npc} came and told you, in the end, or near enough. {He} asked you to meet {him}, and {he} sat across the table, and {he} talked about nothing for an hour, and when {he} got up {he} said: "You should not have done it, you know. I have thought about it a great deal. It would have been kinder." Then {he} went back to them. You sit on at the table. You had thought that you understood what you were buying.

choices.text: Find out what {he} meant

effects.log: You put someone on it, and you find out. It is all as {he} said. It is the most honest anybody has been with you in years, and it comes with a list of names.

choices.text: Let it go by

effects.log: You let it go by. {He} told you what {he} could. You do not know whether that was a warning or a boast, and you will not get another.
